text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency crossed SLO (hosted-api) in us-west-2 — 20m window. Auto-mitigation attempted (route fallback) and failed to bring p99 under target. Links: https://metrics.redwood/internal/d/latency/hosted-api?orgId=1

oncall-maya: seeing the alert, pulling traces now. p95 also trending up. customer impact?

sre-jamie: quick summary: large increase in streaming stalls for long-lived responses (~>2s extra p99 for stream chunks). Paging ops count spiked ~3x. Looks correlated with a prefix-hash change deployed ~30m ago (see deploy id deploy-2026-03-15-09:12).

eng-ryan: confirmed, rollout of prefix-salt v3 at 09:12 UTC. I rolled it in Gradual mode but a config leak caused 40% of requests to use the new salt immediately.

oncall-maya: can we roll back the salt?

eng-ryan: rollback in progress, hitting the cluster API: `kubectl -n runtime set env svc-runtime PREFIX_SALT=v2 --record`

incident-bot: DEPLOY HOOK: rollback triggered by eng-ryan at 1719001500. Running canary check.

infra-sameer: infra note: as salt changed keys, cache namespace rekeyed and caused high cache-miss storm. Backend started paging to KV which increased tail latency. Paging queue fullness on pgo-3 nodes is 85%.

eng-ml-ana: relevance: models with long prefix reuse (chat streaming) are hitting KV more because prefix caching hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 38% after the rehash. That's consistent with p99 spike.

product-zoe: CS flagged customers A and B with streaming glitches. Are we throttling or dropping tokens? Need customer impact summary for PSR.

customer-success-li: I messaged both customers. One reported spiky partial streams, second saw repeated reconnects. They're asking for ETA.

eng-ryan: rollback completed at 1719001620. Canaries show partial recovery but some nodes still show high KV latency. Need cache warmup / proactive prefetch.

oncall-maya: what mitigations besides rollback?

sre-jamie: live mitigations applied: 1) temporary increase of cache TTL for prefix namespace to 6h (to retain already-warmed keys) 2) ramped up prefetch workers by 50% via flag `PREFETCH_WORKERS=48` 3) reduced continuous-batching window to lower in-flight pages.

infra-sameer: added extra paging-buffer memory on pgo-3 by toggling `runtime.paging.buffer_ratio=0.25` on nodes with highest queue. This reduces eviction churn.

eng-ml-ana: I pushed a targeted KV-prefetch patch for top-1000 prefixes (based on recent traffic) to warm them explicitly: `python tools/prefetch.py --top 1000 --region us-west-2`. Started at 1719001705.

oncall-maya: monitoring p95/p99 now.

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE @ 1719001760: p95 back to 450ms (target 500ms), p99 still 2.1s (target 1s). Streaming stall events down 40% from peak. Cache hit-rate now 65%.

customer-success-li: interim message sent to customers: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency caused by cache rehash; rollback and mitigations in progress. We'll update within 30 minutes."

product-zoe: thanks. Track customer token windows impacted and share with AE.

eng-ryan: one anomaly: a small subset (~6%) of requests still routed to older shard set due to stale routing table in edge-proxy. I'm flushing edge-proxies now: `curl -X POST https://edge.internal/flush-routes`

infra-sameer: edge flush completed at 1719001830. Confirmed no stale routes on 98% of edges, a few still in progress.

sre-jamie: next steps and handoff to night oncall: - keep prefetch workers high for next 2 hours - monitor p99, streaming stalls, and paging queue fullness - if p99 > 1.5s for >10m, trigger scale-up of dedicated KV read replicas (runbooks/KV-scale-up) - collect sample traces for top 20 long streams and attach to incident ticket

oncall-maya: assigning to night oncall (sre-oliver). oliver FYI: full context above + runbook link: https://runbooks/redwood/paging-stall. Handoff summary: rollback done, prefetch + TTL + buffer adjustments applied, edge flush started, customers notified. Estimated recovery window: 30-60m but dependent on warmup.

eng-ml-ana: adding probe script to continuously check prefix hit distribution: `./scripts/prefix_hit_probe --interval 30s --log us-west-2.log` — will tag traces with `incident=1719001234`.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Severity P1 -> Escalated. Incident created: INC-1719001234. All actions logged.

customer-success-li: I'll follow up with customers once p99 < 1s for 15m.

product-zoe: please include postmortem owners: eng-ryan (root cause), sre-jamie (mitigations), eng-ml-ana (cache strategy). Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow.

oncall-maya: handoff complete. tagging @sre-oliver and leaving channel. :wave:

sre-jamie: leaving a final note for oncall: observed root cause = prefix-salt rollout triggered cache namespace rekey -> mass cache misses -> backend paging spike -> streaming stalls and p99 breach. Fixes applied: rollback, prefetch warmup, TTL bump, buffer tuning, edge flush. Recommend a controlled rollout plan + pre-warm step in future.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED FOR HANDOFF at 1719001980 (active monitoring continues under INC-1719001234).
